chapter: Mongo Santamaria and early recording sessions
title: After Juilliard: Lloyd Price, Hugo Dickens and Rodgers Grant
summary: After graduating in 1964 Laws plays with Lloyd Price's big band and Hugo Dickens, where Rodgers Grant introduces him to Mongo Santamaria.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I’m going to ask a lot of questions about Mongo. But let’s go back to – do we wrap up – did we wrap up your tenure at Juilliard? You obviously got your degree there. So are you on track now for your goal for your aspiration to perform in a symphony orchestra?

Let’s see. After I finished there, I was actually playing with Mongo after I finished. I had some gigs with Lloyd Price’s big band. I remember one – maybe a month or so. I toured with them. Then I started playing local gigs, dances, with a local band called Hugo Dickens. Hugo Dickens’s band, where I met Willie Bobo and also the piano player who played those gigs. His name was Rodgers Grant. He was the one that introduced me to Mongo. That’s how I got in Mongo’s band. Let me see . . .
When did you graduate from Juilliard?
’64. I’m trying to think of what’s – I’m trying to tell you . . .
